subject: Optimize toolkit — packaging, pricing, and pilot terms
messages:
From: Alex Barnes <alex.barnes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Optimize toolkit — packaging/pricing questions

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We were impressed by the Optimize recommendations you showed (especially the KV-prefix caching ideas). Before we go deeper, procurement wants a clear sense of packaging and expected cost savings so we can compare to an internal optimization effort. A few concrete questions: 

- Do you sell Optimize as an add-on to Hosted API, or is it only part of Dedicated/Private plans?
- For hosted customers, how is Optimize billed — flat subscription, per-model/throughput, or percent-of-savings?
- What are typical uplift metrics you see from batching + L2 KV caching + quantization for encoder-decoder and causal models?
- Any licensing obligations if we run Optimize recommendations in our private infra later?

For context: we have a two-model pilot (one causal, one encoder-decoder) with ~75 req/s aggregate, avg prompt length 360 tokens, peak 300 concurrent users. Target is to cut token cost by ~40% without increasing tail latency > 25 ms.

I've attached a small telemetry sample for your team to eyeball. Procurement will need a price to evaluate — can you send packaging options and any pilot discounts you typically offer?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Sr. ML Platform Eng — Acme Analytics

Alex — thanks for the details and the telemetry sample. High level answers first, then I'll outline a pilot offer and attach our Optimize playbook.

Quick answers:
- Packaging: Optimize is available as a hosted add-on (no infra changes) and as a feature bundle for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted customers get a managed Optimize control plane; Dedicated/Private include the same feature set plus an option to export policy artifacts for on-prem execution under a license.
- Billing: We offer two hosted billing modes for Optimize: 
  1) Subscription + usage: $2,500/month (tooling + analytics + evals) + $0.0008 per optimized inference (metered at token-level equivalence).
  2) Savings-share pilot: for short pilots we can structure a credits-based pilot where we invoice 25% of estimated unit-cost savings (capped) to align incentives.
- Uplift metrics: typical wins depend on model and sequence length, but in your shape (long prompts, steady concurrency) we commonly observe: batching + KV caching => 1.6–2.5x effective throughput; 4-bit quantization (LLM-specific methods) => 1.8–3.5x speedups on Ampere/ADA-class GPUs with ~1–3% quality drift in many workloads. Cumulative gains frequently approach the 40% token-cost reduction you target if policies are tuned.
- Licensing: for Private/Dedicated we provide an export-friendly license (standard enterprise SLA) — you can run the same batching and cache policies on your infra; model weights/licensing are separate.

Pilot proposal (targeted at your two-model pilot):
- 3-month pilot, Optimize Hosted add-on at $1,875/month (25% pilot discount off list) + $0.0006 per optimized inference for the pilot period.
- Commitment: minimum 250M input/output tokens across the pilot (we'll bill on actual usage then reconcile).
- Success criteria: >=30% token-cost reduction and no >25ms tail latency increase for p95.
- Optional SRE assist: 8 hours of SE time (Rishi) to tune policies during onboarding (included).

I've attached the Optimize_Playbook_v1.pdf with recommended batching/cache presets and quantization caveats. Can we jump on a 30-min call to walk through and confirm procurement items? If helpful, we can propose a mutual action plan and a DocuSign to expedite.

Thanks — cc'ing Rishi and Laura for visibility.

Best,

Alex — quick technical note to supplement Marissa's email:

- For your causal model (75 req/s, long prompts) I recommend starting with a dynamic batching window tuned to a 12–25 ms target latency. That typically gives 1.8–2.2x token throughput with negligible quality impact.
- KV-prefix caching works very well when users have repeated prefixes; if your workload has high prompt repetition for system/system+user prefixes we can often drop inference compute by 25–45%.
- Quantization: for decoder-only models we suggest per-channel 4-bit quant (q4_0/q4_1 style) as a first pass; test in a shadow environment because some generation tasks (very open-ended) show higher calibration drift. We provide an automated eval harness inside Optimize to compare output deltas and flag regressions.
- Canary plan: run Optimize policies in shadow mode for 2 days, then a 10% traffic canary for 48 hours before full rollout. We'll instrument evaluation metrics (per-prompt quality, p95 latency, token-cost) and stop on regression flags.

Happy to run the initial profiling if you share a 24–72 hour trace — we can provide concrete expected $/token numbers.

—Rishi
Staff Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Marissa, Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the playbook. A few follow-ups from procurement and platform budgeting: 

1) Pilot discount: we usually need larger pilot discounts to justify vendor pilots vs internal work. Can Redwood do 30% off list for 3 months (subscription fee only)?
2) Metering clarity: we need a precise definition for "optimized inference" (is it per token after batching/merged requests? What about cached hits?). Procurement is concerned about double-billing for cache hits.
3) SLA & rollback: if Optimize policies cause a degradation we need a defined rollback SLA and credit schedule.

We can sign quickly if those three items are clarified. Also, can you share the mutual action plan PDF with milestones and a draft DocuSign?

Alex

Alex — appreciate the points. Proposal below addresses each procurement ask plus a practical concession so we can get the pilot running: 

1) Pilot discount: we can increase to a 25% subscription discount plus waived first-month subscription if you sign within five business days. (We have to balance commercial precedent and SE time.)

2) Metering definition: 
- "Optimized inference" = billed per inference-equivalent token emitted by the model after any runtime batching/merging. Cache hits (where the response is served entirely from a cached KV entry and no model compute is invoked) are not billed as optimized inferences. Partial cache-hit paths that still trigger generation are billed on emitted tokens. We will include a sample billing report schema in the MAP.

3) SLA & rollback: 
- Rollback SLA: if post-canary we observe regression flags (per your agreed eval set) that exceed threshold we will roll the policy back within 2 business hours and open a high-priority incident.
- Credits: if an outage or regression caused by Optimize lasts >4 hours and materially breaches p95 latency/quality thresholds, we will apply a pro-rated credit up to 10% of that month’s subscription fee.

Mutual action plan: attached is MAP_Acme_Optimize_3mo.pdf with milestones, owners, and the DocuSign link for signature. Key bullets: 
- Week 0–1: telemetry ingest + profiling (Rishi)
- Week 2: shadow run + evaluation (metrics: token-cost delta, p95 latency, quality delta)
- Week 3: 10% canary + rollback validation
- Week 4–12: ramp to production + weekly checkpoints

Commercial compromise: 25% subscription discount (pilot), $0.0006 per optimized inference, and 8 SE hours included. After pilot, standard list resumes (or we can provide Dedicated pricing if you want a committed capacity discount).

If that sounds acceptable I can send the DocuSign now and we’ll book Rishi for profiling next week. Laura is cc'd for commercial approval — fyi she has signed off on the pilot concession.

Best,
Marissa Cole
